GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2020-10-26T23:13:21Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: aggressive JIT recompilation with equal-but-not-identical args
Description: I'm having an issue with a JIT-compiled function being recompiled at every run. This seems to happen whenever an argument set as static is not _identical_ to its previous value (in the sense of `is` or `id(arg)`), rather than when it is not _equal_ to its previous value (in the sense of `==`).

Is this an expected behavior / a limitation of the compilation model?

---

As a simple example, consider:

```python
@jax.partial(jax.jit, static_argnums=(0,))
def dummy_add_fn(dummy, x):
    return x + 1
```

If we run + profile this, we find that whenever the identity of `dummy` changes, the function recompiles.

```python
dummy_arg = [0]
real_arg = jnp.zeros((3,))
with jax.profiler.TraceContext("Run 1"):
    dummy_add_fn(dummy_arg, real_arg)  # <- JIT compilation
with jax.profiler.TraceContext("Run 2"):
    dummy_add_fn(dummy_arg, real_arg)  # <- no compilation

dummy_arg = [0]
with jax.profiler.TraceContext("Run 3"):
    dummy_add_fn(dummy_arg, real_arg)  # <- compiles again
```

This happens even though `[0] == [0]`.
